_: The families, in the order they should be drawn, one sentence each, and
the style a sitting in one runs under when nothing below it says otherwise.
aim  what a sitting in this family is FOR when nobody chose: 'teach' in
a family of coursework, where the mathematics is done properly and
the person does the step; 'build' in a family of work, where the
tutor writes it and reports what it changed. A workspace overrides
it in its own tutorboard.json, and a sitting overrides that. It is
not a mode and it is not a registry: `course/config.aim_for` is the
one place the precedence lives.
A DEFAULT HERE IS A STYLE AND NEVER AN INSTRUCTION TO WRITE CODE.
'build' says what a sitting in this family is usually for; it does
not on its own make a sitting nobody chose into one where the tutor
writes the code. A sentence about a directory is not a repository
asking in writing, and writing somebody's code for them when they
wanted to learn it is the one failure the next card cannot undo. So
`aim_for` drops a doing default and the sitting runs on stance;
a tap, or an aim in a workspace's own tutorboard.json, is honoured
exactly as written. A 'teach' default applies as it always has.
That is ALL this file holds. It does not list the workspaces. A workspace
is a second-level directory that holds tutorboard.json, AI_INSTRUCTIONS.md
or live/ -- discovered, never registered -- because a file that has to be
edited when a directory is made is the registry this system refuses to
have. Making a new course is `mkdir courses/Topology`, and the front door
draws it on the next poll.
Two flags, and both mean 'not a workspace you can be taught in':
vendor  somebody else's repositories, tracked by pointer. Discovery
skips the family entirely -- nothing in it is the person's to
be graded on.
tool    the family directory IS the thing, with no workspaces under it.
`board/` is the tutoring board's own source. It is drawn on the
atlas because it is real work, and it is not offered as a
subject because it is what does the offering.
